```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
```

## Icons as markers

The [fontawesome package](https://rstudio.github.io/fontawesome/) provides SVG
icons that can be used in markers and tooltips. These are the original R and
Python examples, with the same data and colors. Embedding the SVG directly keeps
the icons sharp and avoids an intermediate PNG file.

```{r svg-markers}
library(fontawesome)

set.seed(123)
df <- data.frame(
  a = round(rnorm(10), 2),
  b = round(rnorm(10), 2)
)

fa_to_data_uri <- function(name, fill, width = 22) {
  size <- paste0(width, "px")
  icon <- fontawesome::fa(name, fill = fill, width = size, height = size)
  svg <- as.character(icon)
  # Standalone images need an XML namespace and intrinsic pixel dimensions.
  svg <- sub(
    "<svg",
    sprintf(
      '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="%s" height="%s"',
      width,
      width
    ),
    svg,
    fixed = TRUE
  )
  svg <- sub(
    'preserveAspectRatio="none"',
    'preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"',
    svg,
    fixed = TRUE
  )
  paste0(
    "data:image/svg+xml,",
    utils::URLencode(svg, reserved = TRUE)
  )
}

# Reuse the same colors in markers, series and tooltips.
rcol <- "#4C83B6"
pcol <- "#3CAB48"
rproj <- fa_to_data_uri("r-project", fill = rcol)
pthon <- fa_to_data_uri("python", fill = pcol)

highchart() |>
  hc_title(text = "Font Awesome icons") |>
  hc_add_series(
    df,
    "scatter",
    hcaes(a, b),
    name = "R icons",
    color = rcol,
    marker = list(symbol = paste0("url(", rproj, ")")),
    icon = as.character(fontawesome::fa(
      "r-project",
      fill = rcol,
      height = "15px",
      vertical_align = "middle"
    ))
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    df,
    "scatter",
    hcaes(b, a),
    name = "Python icons",
    color = pcol,
    marker = list(symbol = paste0("url(", pthon, ")")),
    icon = as.character(fontawesome::fa(
      "python",
      fill = pcol,
      height = "15px",
      vertical_align = "middle"
    ))
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    useHTML = TRUE,
    pointFormat = paste0(
      "<b>",
      "{series.options.icon} ",
      "[{point.x}, {point.y}]",
      "</b>"
    )
  )
```

## Count with pictograms

This example, inspired by [waffle](https://github.com/hrbrmstr/waffle), uses the
original food categories, counts and colors. Each symbol represents one unit.

```{r item-icons}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

df2 <- tibble(
  type = c("fruit", "samminch", "pizza"),
  amount = c(46, 54, 80),
  faico = c("apple", "bread-slice", "pizza-slice"),
  col = c("#d35400", "#907E4D", "#F89101")
)

df2

df2 <- df2 |>
  mutate(
    uri = map2_chr(faico, col, ~ fa_to_data_uri(.x, fill = .y)),
    marker = map(uri, ~ list(symbol = paste0("url(", .x, ")")))
  )

hchart(
  df2,
  "item",
  hcaes(name = type, y = amount),
  name = "What I eat",
  showInLegend = TRUE
) |>
  hc_legend(labelFormat = "{name} <span style='opacity: 0.4'>{y}</span>") |>
  hc_colors(pull(df2, col))
```

See the [Highcharts item chart guide](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-and-series-types/item-chart)
for other layouts and symbol options.
